input_description: Gadget-4 SubLink merger tree for the 'gadget4-dust' simulation: single-file trees.hdf5 (1.1 GB), 194,957 trees, ~8.4 million halos, 128 snapshots, 35 Mpc/h box, SUBFIND_HBT halo finder, cosmology Omega=0.321 OmegaLambda=0.679 h=0.6688
issues_encountered: TreeDescendant misidentified as global flat-array index: early driver versions subtracted StartOffset to obtain tree-local indices, which was correct only for Tree0 (StartOffset=0) but silently corrupted all other trees.
TreeFirstProgenitor/TreeNextProgenitor point forward in time in Gadget-4 (opposite to SAGE convention) and contain cross-tree references; they cannot be used directly.
TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup/TreeNextHaloInFOFgroup contain cross-tree pointers that cannot be resolved within a single tree slice.
~0.2% of halos have same-snapshot TreeDescendant values (intra-snapshot FOF mergers), violating the SAGE requirement that Descendant must point strictly forward in time.
Forest reconstruction via global pointer-jumping (attempted in v3) was also incorrect because it depended on the false global-index assumption.
resolutions: Verified tree-local interpretation by checking Trees 0-4: under local interpretation, zero backward desc links exist in all trees; under global interpretation, 607,938 spurious backward links appear in Tree1 alone. Final driver (v4) uses TreeDescendant values as-is (no offset subtraction): they are already in [0, Length) or -1.
Discarded TreeFirstProgenitor and TreeNextProgenitor; reconstructed FirstProgenitor/NextProgenitor by inverting the resolved Descendant array (sort by SubhaloLen descending, vectorised, O(N log N)).
Discarded TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup and TreeNextHaloInFOFgroup; reconstructed FirstHaloInFOFGroup/NextHaloInFOFGroup from (SnapNum, GroupNr) grouping (vectorised lexsort + cumsum, O(N log N)).
Added _resolve_same_snap_desc() that iteratively follows same-snapshot desc links (up to 10 hops per halo, using original values for each hop) until a cross-snapshot or -1 link is reached.
Reverted to one-Gadget4-tree = one-SAGE-tree (no forest reconstruction); processes each tree as an independent slice, yielding 194,957 SAGE trees.
